content.value_statement: Unclear requirements can lead to premature implementation and missing architecture decisions. This skill guides structured discovery and creates Mermaid-based design catalogs for shared planning.
actual_capabilities: Guides requirements discovery through focused questions and validation checkpoints.
Uses EventStorming to map commands, events, actors, systems, aggregates, and hotspots.
Creates Mermaid diagrams for big-picture flows, processes, ERDs, states, and sequences.
Organizes artifacts under a standard docs/design-catalog structure.
Keeps design artifacts conceptual and avoids implementation-specific deliverables.
Embeds diagram content into a catalog README for easier review.
limitations: It does not generate production code, database migrations, or deployment guides.
It depends on user answers for accurate requirements and constraints.
It is best for new systems or early planning, not active implementation changes.
It limits detailed diagrams to critical processes, entities, and flows.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product System
use_cases.description: Turn an early product idea into requirements, event flows, and architecture diagrams before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Align Engineering Teams
use_cases.description: Create a shared design catalog that captures business events, process boundaries, and open architectural hotspots.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation Planning
use_cases.description: Build conceptual artifacts that can feed later task planning without locking in code or deployment details too early.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Design Catalog
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a short product idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the system-design skill to help me design a system for this idea: [describe the product]. Ask me the first requirements question.

prompt_templates.title: Map Business Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Use EventStorming to identify commands, events, actors, external systems, and hotspots for [system]. Build the big-picture Mermaid diagram.

prompt_templates.title: Detail Critical Processes
prompt_templates.scenario: Zoom into risky or high-value workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the big-picture design and choose the 2 to 4 most critical processes. For each one, create a Mermaid process diagram and validate it with me.

prompt_templates.title: Assemble a Complete Catalog
prompt_templates.scenario: Finish the design catalog for team review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Complete the system design catalog with requirements, big-picture events, process diagrams, conceptual data models, state charts, sequence diagrams, and an embedded README.

output_examples.input: Design an appointment booking platform for clinics.
output_examples.output: A design catalog with requirements, a big-picture EventStorming timeline, booking and cancellation process diagrams, conceptual patient and appointment entities, and key scheduling hotspots.

output_examples.input: Help our team align on a marketplace architecture before coding.
output_examples.output: A shared catalog that shows buyer and seller events, payment and fulfillment integrations, core entity relationships, order state transitions, and questions that need decisions.

output_examples.input: Turn our requirements notes into architecture artifacts.
output_examples.output: Structured requirements, Mermaid diagrams for critical flows, a navigation README, and a focused list of unresolved design choices.

best_practices: Answer the discovery questions with real constraints, user roles, and success criteria.
Review each phase before moving forward so downstream diagrams stay accurate.
Use hotspots for uncertain decisions instead of forcing premature technology choices.
anti_patterns: Skipping questions and asking for a complete architecture from vague requirements.
Using the skill to write production code, deployment plans, or database migrations.
Trying to diagram every possible workflow instead of focusing on critical flows.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a structured design catalog with requirements, EventStorming diagrams, conceptual data models, state charts, sequence diagrams, and a README.

faq.question: Does it choose my technology stack?
faq.answer: No. It asks about constraints and marks unresolved technical choices as hotspots unless you already provided the stack.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this for existing systems?
faq.answer: It is strongest for new systems and early architecture planning. Existing implementation work may need a different workflow.

faq.question: Why does it use EventStorming?
faq.answer: EventStorming helps teams identify business events, triggers, actors, external systems, data changes, and uncertainty before implementation.

faq.question: Does it produce implementation tasks?
faq.answer: No. It stops at conceptual design and can provide context for a separate implementation planning workflow.
